passages.title: OOP — Encapsulation
passages.text: Encapsulation is the bundling of data and the methods that operate on that data within a single unit called a class. It restricts direct access to an object's internal state and prevents unintended interference or misuse of the data.

passages.title: OOP — Inheritance
passages.text: Inheritance allows a class to acquire the properties and methods of another class. The child class extends the parent class and can override inherited methods to provide specialised behaviour while reusing existing code.

passages.title: Algorithms
passages.text: An algorithm is a finite sequence of well-defined instructions that solves a computational problem. Algorithms are evaluated on their time complexity and space complexity to determine their efficiency at scale.

passages.title: Data Structures
passages.text: A data structure is a way of organising and storing data so it can be accessed and modified efficiently. Common structures include arrays, linked lists, stacks, queues, trees, and hash tables.
